I got a call from a PI firm owner last week.

He was furious.

$57,000 spent on marketing in 18 months.
3 different agencies.
12 signed cases total.

That's $4,750 per case.

For a practice area where the average case is worth $40K+, that math should work.

But here's what actually happened:

Agency 1 promised 20 qualified leads per month.
Delivered 3.
No call tracking installed.
No reporting beyond a monthly email saying "we're optimizing."

Agency 2 sent beautiful reports.
Clicks up 47%.
CTR up 22%.
Cases? Down.

They were optimizing for metrics that don't pay the bills.

Agency 3 is where it got truly insane.
They ran ads to the wrong zip code — 140 miles away from the firm's office — for FOUR MONTHS.
Billed $2,000/month the entire time.
Nobody caught it until the firm owner logged into Google Ads himself.

The common thread?

None of them tracked signed cases.

Not leads.
Not calls.
Not consultations.

Signed. Cases.

Before you hire any agency, ask three things:

1. "How do you define a lead?" — If they say clicks or form fills without qualification, run.

2. "What's my cost per signed case?" — If they don't track it or say "that's on your intake team," run.

3. "Can I access all accounts?" — If they say no or hesitate, run.

Good agencies welcome accountability.

Bad ones hide behind impressions and CTR.

The difference is $57,000.

Unpopular opinion:

If your marketing agency can't tell you the cost per SIGNED CASE, fire them.

I don't care how good the reports look.
I don't care if clicks are up.
I don't care about CTR or Quality Score or impressions.

A law firm owner just spent $57K across 3 agencies.

12 signed cases.

$4,750 per case.

Agency 1: "We delivered 47 leads!"
3 answered the phone.

Agency 2: "CTR is up 22%!"
Cases are down.

Agency 3: Ran ads to the wrong zip code for 4 months.
Charged $2K/month anyway.

The marketing industry has convinced law firms that "lead generation" is the goal.

It's not.

Signed cases are the goal.

If your agency doesn't measure that — or worse, says "that's not our job" — you're paying someone to waste your money with extra steps.

Your agency should know:
- Cost per signed case
- Conversion rate from call to consult
- Conversion rate from consult to signed
- Which campaigns are signing cases (not just generating clicks)

Anything less is a vanity metrics factory.

SUBJECT: The $57,000 lesson every law firm owner needs to read

OPENING:
A criminal defense attorney called me last week. He was furious. He'd spent $57,000 on marketing in 18 months across three different agencies. Total signed cases? 12. That's $4,750 per case. For a practice area where cases are worth $8K-$25K, that math is brutal.

STORY:
Agency 1: Promised 20 leads/month, delivered 3, no call tracking, no reporting beyond "we're optimizing."
Agency 2: Beautiful reports. Clicks up 47%, CTR up 22%, cases down. Classic vanity metrics trap.
Agency 3: Ran ads to the wrong zip code — 140 miles away — for 4 months. Billed $2K/month the whole time.

THE PATTERN:
None measured signed cases. They tracked impressions, clicks, form fills, CTR — everything except revenue.

THE FRAMEWORK:
Before you hire any agency, ask:
1. How do you define a lead? (If clicks = run)
2. What's my cost per signed case? (If they don't know = run)
3. Can I access all accounts? (If no = run)

THE MATH:
Let's say you're a PI firm. Average case value: $40K. If your cost per signed case is under $2K, you're printing money. If it's $4,750 like this firm, you're bleeding.

ACTION STEPS:
- Log into your Google Ads account TODAY (if you don't have access, demand it)
- Install call tracking this week (CallRail, $45/month)
- Ask your agency for cost per signed case — not cost per lead
- If they can't answer, start interviewing replacements

CLOSING:
Good agencies welcome accountability. Bad ones hide behind impressions. The difference is $57,000.
